full_judgment:
Mr. Mohammad Fazlul Karim, J.: This petition for leave to appeal at the instance of the petitioner is directed against the judgment and order dated 30.01.2006 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3845 of 2005 discharging the Rule and vacating the order of stay of the proceedings of C.A. Case No.1549C of 2004 dated 02.06.2004 filed under Sections 406/420 of the Penal Code corresponding to Petition Case No.32I of 2004 pending before the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate, Khulna. 

 2. The facts of the case, in short, are that the complainant respondent lodged the complaint impleading the accused petitioner alleging that marriage was solemnized in between the complainant and the, accused petitioner on 29.09.1978 and 3 daughters were born during the wedlock, eldest is at the age of 24 and the youngest is at the age of 16. The accused petitioner appeared in this case and was enlarged on bail. It appears from the order sheet that when the Rule was obtained, charge was framed against the accused petitioner under Section 420 of the Penal Code. 

 3. The complainant for his business purpose usually travelled Dhaka, North Bengal and other places of Bangladesh and for maintaining the family affairs, opened 'Saving Account No.5721 in Agrani Bank, Daulatpur Branch and sent Tk.5,80,000.00 and also Tk.3,50,000.00 i.e. the money received from house rent, to the accused petitioner. The accused petitioner sold the landed property of the complainant purchased in the name of the accused petitioner at a cost of Tk.I3,25,000.00 and the accused petitioner gave Tk.3,00,000.00 to one Tipu Sultan to send younger brother of the accused petitioner, Sheikh Shahin to U.S.A. in 1996. In 1978 the complainant purchased 10 decimals of land with a two unite one storied building which the complainant gradually raised to 5 storied building where the complainant used to reside with his family members. The complainant gave with condition to return the same to accused petitioner 25% of 10 decimals of land with a pucca structure of the accused petitioner and remaining 75% to 3 daughters of the complainant. The daughters returned the property as per terms of the gift but the wife i.e. the accused petitioner did not return the said property. When the said property and money were demanded the accused petitioner with hired gonda elements, driven out the complainant from the said property. The complainant served a legal notice. The .complainant for his safety, instituted Petition Case No.116 of 2004 which case was enquired and the officer-in-charge reported finding troth of the complaint case. At the time of enquiry, accused petitioner showed a false divorce letter, G.D. Entry No.75 on 02.03.2004 was also made against the accused petitioner. The complainant also filed Petition Case No.180 of 2004 under Section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure against the accused petitioner. 

 4. Mr. M. Moksadul Islam, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner submitted that the High Court Division failed to apply its judicial minds in assessing the evidence and materials on record and the provision of law applicable thereto and to appreciate the facts and circumstances of the case in its true perspective; that the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division has seriously affected the petitioner's authority and lawful obligation and requires this Court's protection by way of setting aside the said impugned order. The learned Advocate further submitted that once any money is given to a partner of a marriage it belongs him/her and none can bring any action under Section 420 of the Penal Code; that the petition case has been filed stating the petitioner as his wife and neither the husband nor the wife can bring any criminal action against each other for breach of the contractual delegation. The learned Advocate submitted that none of the counts of allegations made by, respondent No.2 come under the purview of Section 420 of the Penal Code and the High Court Division erred in law in discharging the Rule as there cannot be any allegation against any partner of a marriage under Section 420 of the Penal Code. 

 5. Admittedly, the money was received by the accused petitioner, during continuation of the marriage, for maintaining the family but there is allegation that the accused petitioner after breaking the mutual trust misappropriated the huge amount given to her by the complainant, the question of exhausting the money for maintaining the family does not hold good. It appears that the accused petitioner betraying the mutual trust which is the basis of maintaining a family bondage of husband and wife relation misappropriated the entire case and misappropriated the landed property. 

 6. It further appears that the accused petitioner did not invoke the provision of Section 241A of the Code of Criminal Procedure nor moved the Sessions Judge, under Section 439A of the Code of Criminal Procedure against framing charge. It has been settled that when the matter at the stage of taking deposition, the case should not be quashed unless the same is on preposterous facts apparent to the complaint petition.
